newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CSE seeks clarification from Seylan.
newsitem.headline: CSE seeks clarification from Seylan.

text.p: The Colombo Stock Exchange said on Thursday it was writing to Seylan Bank Ltd seeking clarification about a local newspaper report that an official at an unidentified bank was questioned over foreign exchange fraud.
"We are writing to Seylan to clarify whether they are the bank referred to, and if so what the implications on the bank would be," said exchange director-general Dillon Moldrich.
No comment was available from Seylan Bank.

On Wednesday, the state-owned Daily News said a top official at a private bank was questioned by police over a foreign exchange fraud. The newspaper did not identify the bank and police and the Central Bank have declined comment.

The Daily News said on Thursday police were offering a 750,000 rupee reward for information leading to the arrest of two private bank employees in connection with embezzlement of 12.8 million rupees ($220,689).
The newspaper identified the employees but not the bank.

"Trading of (Seylan's) share will continue until we get the bank's clarification, but we will be keeping a close tab on movements," Moldrich said. The stock was trading at 21.50 rupees on Thursday, down from 22.25 rupees on Wednesday.
Brokers said the newspaper report pressured the stock. ($1 = 58 rupees)
